messages.subject: Multinomial mixed effects
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I wonder if anyone can offer some advice/script sharing on mixed effects
multinomial regression? I apologise that this has been asked before, but no
clear solution was available at the time and I'm aware that a number of
packages have been developed since then.

My data is from a word learning experiment, and my difficulty is with data
from a definitions task which is scored 0-3 depending on the richness of
semantic information provided. I have three fixed effects (a context
manipulation, test point, vocabulary ability), and have been largely
attempting maximally specified random effects structures throughout the
rest of the data analysis.

Does anyone have some experience with analysing similar data that they
would be happy to share please? Or guidance towards helpful resources?
Other suggestions for analysis approaches also very welcome.

Many thanks in advance,
Emma

messages.subject: Re: Multinomial mixed effects
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emma,

yes this has been discussed before.  You can find my previous response
here:

  https://mailman.ucsd.edu/pipermail/ling-r-lang-l/2015-May/000794.html

See also the rest of that thread.

The solution is basically to do a ordered logistic regression (I’m
assuming that your scores are ordered).  One package that allows you to
do this is called ordinal.  If you want a Bayesian variant you could use
the package MCMCglmm but that’s a little harder to use.

Hope that helps,

  Titus
